clue.text: At Masherbrum weep convulsively about hotel being rubbish

parts.note: Masherbrum, a Karakoram peak, was surveyed as K1, with the one written as the letter I

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for weeping is read backwards

parts.note: to weep convulsively is to sob
H is Hotel in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A climber on a Himalayan peak breaks down in tears, finding the hotel there dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SOB into BOS.
explanation.definitionFit: An old slang word for nonsense, now mostly heard in 'put the kibosh on'.

clue.text: Ken eviscerated boorish Australian critic

indicators.note: eviscerated means gutted, so only the outside letters of the name are kept

parts.note: an ocker is Australian slang for an uncouth, loud Australian

explanation.surface: Some man named Ken savages a crude Australian reviewer.
explanation.definitionFit: A knocker is someone who habitually finds fault, a carping detractor.

clue.text: Character 8, fool and Scotsman boarding transport

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the fool and the Scot go inside the vehicle

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport
an ass is a fool
Ian is a stock Scottish man's name in crosswords

explanation.surface: A clown and a Scot climb aboard a coach, as if casting a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 down supplies OF SHAKESPEARE, so 'Character 8' is a character of Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Bassianus is the Emperor's brother in Titus Andronicus, a Shakespeare play.

clue.text: Sons back the Big Band Sound

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
in rugby the wings are among the backs, so a wing is a kind of back

explanation.surface: Musicians' sons return to the jazz-orchestra style of their parents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a direction to reverse, but it is a rugby position: the wing plays in the back line.
explanation.definitionFit: Swing is the jazz style played by the big bands of the 1930s and 40s.

clue.text: Character 8 lasts in sumo wrestling among island people

indicators.note: among means set in the middle of the island-and-people string

parts.note: men means people

indicators.note: lasts in points to the final letter of each of the two following words

explanation.surface: Islanders take part in sumo wrestling bouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lasts in' takes O and G, the final letters of 'sumo' and 'wrestling'; 'among' sets them inside I + MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Imogen is the heroine of Cymbeline, so she is a character of Shakespeare.

clue.text: Fruit from these branches torn out in riotous brawl

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters are placed inside the brawl word

parts.note: a melee is a confused, riotous fight

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the word torn are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Boughs get ripped off a tree during a wild punch-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal for 'torn', and 'in' is a container signal, not a link; 'riotous' belongs to the brawl, not the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The melon tree is the papaya, whose large fruits hang from it.

clue.text: Feasible idea comes about with character 8

indicators.note: comes about means goes around, so the workable idea surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: a goer is a scheme that is workable, one that will go ahead

explanation.surface: A workable notion arrives involving a Shakespeare role.
explanation.definitionFit: Gower, the medieval poet, is the Chorus figure in Pericles, a character of Shakespeare.

clue.text: This cancels out meal served up where companion refused fish

indicators.note: served up, in a down clue, means the remaining letters are read upwards
refused means turned away, so the companion's letters are dropped from the meal

parts.note: lunch is a meal
CH stands for Companion of Honour
a ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A lunch is sent back because the diner's partner turned down the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refused' takes CH from LUNCH to leave LUN, and 'served up' makes it NUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Nulling is the act of cancelling or making void, so it is something that cancels out.

clue.text: See 23
Pious use oars drawn back with vessel almost loaded

indicators.note: drawn back means the rowing word runs backwards

parts.note: to use oars is to row
a ship is a vessel

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: full means loaded

explanation.surface: Devout souls pull back on their oars, the boat nearly full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn back' turns ROW into WOR, and 'almost' cuts FULL to FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Worshipful means full of reverence or devotion, as a pious person is.

clue.text: Wife sick in mind

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: A wife is mentally unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Will is the mind's power to decide, as in 'a mind of one's own'; it is also the bard's first name.

clue.text: Mountain sport no good after having succeeded at Godwin-Austen?

indicators.note: after places the no-good letters behind the rest

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
Mount Godwin-Austen is K2, with the two written as the Roman numeral II

explanation.surface: A climber's sport proves useless after conquering K2.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing is sliding downhill on skis, the classic sport of snowy slopes.

clue.text: Solo physician, in good health, left support on stair

parts.note: Han Solo is the Star Wars smuggler
Dr is short for doctor, a physician
A1 means in first-class condition, with the one written as I

explanation.surface: A lone doctor, fit and well, has abandoned a means of support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solo' looks like 'alone', but it is Han Solo's surname, giving his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A handrail is the rail gripped for steadiness when climbing a staircase.

clue.text: 18's little cousin an architect

definitions.meaning: a tiny songbird, a small relative of the bird at 18
Sir Christopher ... designed St Paul's Cathedral

explanation.surface: A tiny relation of a big white bird is also a building designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a very small brown bird and the architect of St Paul's share this name.

clue.text: Harnessing gravitational pull, UK feet are out to find shelter

indicators.note: harnessing means holding within, so the rearranged letters take in the gravity symbol
out signals the letters of the three words are put in a new order

parts.note: g is the physics symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: Using gravity's pull, British walkers set off in search of somewhere safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges UKFEETARE, which 'Harnessing' wraps round G.
explanation.definitionFit: To take refuge is to seek safety or a sheltered place, an idiom for finding cover.

clue.text: An essential travel item, BA let it go astray

indicators.note: astray means wandering off course, so the letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: British Airways lost a vital piece of luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: A washbag for toothbrush and soap is a staple of any traveller's luggage.

clue.text: Onslaught gives everyone lift in following United team

parts.note: U is short for United in team names

indicators.note: in places the lifted word inside the team word

parts.note: a side is a team

indicators.note: lift, in a down clue, means the everyone word is raised to read upwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A supportive crowd boosts a football side named United.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'lift' means the word for everyone reads upwards, and 'in' sets it inside the team word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusillade is a burst of gunfire, or by extension a sustained barrage of attack.

clue.text: Stuff on coniferous trees comes to Magazine One

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, means the material comes after the trees

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees
tissue is material, stuff

explanation.surface: Material placed on fir trees arrives at a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: Magazines are printed on paper from trees like these, which is the surface link.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine's first issue is its number one, the debut edition.

clue.text: Current artist hot sun bathes got up too quickly

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: got up, in a down clue, means the letters are read upwards
bathes means wraps round, as sunlight bathes a figure

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter sunbathing in the heat jumps up far too fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bathes' puts RA inside HSUN to give HSURAN; 'got up' turns it to NARUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a rush means acting hastily, with undue speed.

clue.text: Sweet name 8 workers' leader used in convalescent home

indicators.note: used in means the leading letter goes inside the recovery-home word

parts.note: a san is short for sanatorium, a place to recover

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A union leader's affectionate nickname gets used in a nursing home.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Jonson called Shakespeare the 'Sweet Swan of Avon', so 'Sweet name 8' is a name for Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonson's tribute poem names the bard a graceful river bird of his home town Stratford.

clue.text: Regularly able to leave one country for another

indicators.note: to leave means those picked letters are removed

parts.note: Australia is a country

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word able

explanation.surface: Fit people routinely emigrate from one nation to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes A and L from 'able'; 'to leave' removes them from AUSTRALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a European nation, so it is a second country beside the first.

clue.text: New entertainment by brilliant old Persian character 8

indicators.note: entertainment by means the new letter is held as a guest within the bright word

parts.note: gay in an older sense means bright and showy
the Medes were an ancient people of Persia

explanation.surface: A dazzling ancient Persian provides a fresh show.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganymede is the alias Rosalind takes in As You Like It, a character of Shakespeare.

clue.text: Unknown colleagues topped the star from 'Stars on Sunday'

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown

indicators.note: topped means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: mates are colleagues

explanation.surface: Anonymous co-workers beat the presenter of a TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: Stars on Sunday was a British religious TV show of the 1970s, presented by Jess Yates.
explanation.definitionFit: Jess Yates fronted the programme, so he was its main on-screen figure.

clue.text: Nasty old woman saving money for slingback shoe

indicators.note: slingback splits as sling back, meaning the whole is thrown backwards
saving means keeping inside, so the hag holds the money

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman
the sol is the currency of Peru

explanation.surface: A spiteful old woman hoards cash to buy herself an open-heeled shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' puts SOL in HAG to give HSOLAG, which 'slingback' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A galosh is a rubber overshoe worn in wet weather, a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Start with Garrick, then look to live in House 8

indicators.note: start with means take the opening letter of the name

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Begin with the actor David Garrick, then aim to live in Shakespeare's theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Garrick was an 18th-century actor famous for Shakespeare roles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Globe was the playhouse of Shakespeare's company, his theatrical home.

parts.note: the entries at 10 and 1 down give the bard's first name and a slang word for breasts; read that way, a sculpted head and shoulders

explanation.walkthrough: 10 is WILL and 1 down is KNOCKER, slang for breasts, which make a bust; WILL is Shakespeare, so 'Will's knockers' is his bust.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders, and statues of the bard are common.

clue.text: Practice 9 8 disturbing to lad impressed by composer

indicators.note: impressed by means pressed inside, so the jumble goes into the composer's name

parts.note: John Barry composed the James Bond film scores

indicators.note: disturbing means the letters of to lad are jumbled

explanation.surface: A worshipful practice disturbs a boy who is impressed by a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition combines entries 9 and 8: worship of the Bard. 'disturbing' jumbles 'to lad' and 'impressed by' sets it within the composer's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Bardolatry is excessive veneration of the Bard, the cult of reverence for Shakespeare.

clue.text: Confronts criminal as previously on heroin

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, means the rest follows the heroin letter

parts.note: H is slang for heroin
ago means previously

explanation.surface: Someone tackles a crook, as before, while high on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage, to 'have a go' is to tackle a criminal; the clue's 'Confronts' is the 'has' form.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the public who has a go tackles a wrongdoer, an idiom for standing up to them.

clue.text: The Lenaean's character 8

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, meaning the words contain the answer

explanation.surface: A Lenaean festival player has a Shakespeare role.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lenaea was an ancient Athenian drama festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Helena is a lover in A Midsummer Night's Dream, a character of Shakespeare.
